title: AI adoption among professional developers, 2023-2026
alt_text: Line chart. Share of professional developers using AI tools rose from 44.1% in 2023 to 63.3% in 2024 and 80.8% in 2025; 'plan to use' fell from 26.0% to 4.6%. 2026 (86.1%) is shown after a dashed series break because the question changed. Grey dropout bounds widen to 62.1-85.3% in 2025 and 56.4-90.9% in 2026.

title: Use rises while favourability and trust fall
alt_text: Line chart 2023-2025 with 2026 after a series break. Use among professional developers: 44.1% to 80.8%. Among users, favourable: 84.9% to 73.1% (2026: 62.5%); trust in accuracy: 46.2% to 38.4%; distrust: 25.1% to 37.9%. Distrust and trust are nearly equal by 2025.

title: Use-trust paradox within experience, role and region subgroups
alt_text: Dot-and-whisker chart of 2023-to-2025 changes by subgroup. Use rose by 21.9 to 42.2 points in every subgroup; distrust rose significantly in 18 of 18 subgroups; trust fell significantly in 12 of 18. Subgroups where the trust fall was not significant: 0-4 yrs, MENA, Afg. & Pakistan, South Asia, Management / exec / product, Ops / infra / security / support, Student.

title: Experience gradient in trust, distrust and favourability
alt_text: Three-panel line chart by years of coding experience. In every year 2023-2025, developers with 20+ years trust AI accuracy less than those with 0-4 years (gap -7.2 points in 2023, -9.2 in 2025) and distrust it more (gap 8.4 and 8.9); the gap did not widen significantly (interaction p = 0.51). Favourability shows no experience gap 2023-2025; in 2026 seniors are 11.7 points more favourable.

title: Favourability among AI users by age, experience, role and region
alt_text: Dumbbell chart of favourable share among AI users in 2023 and 2025 with 2026 triangles. Favourability fell significantly in all 23 subgroups between 2023 and 2025, by -2.7 (South Asia) to -17.9 points; 2026 values are lower again but use a relabelled scale.

title: Perceived complex-task capability and its link to favourability
alt_text: Bar chart. Share of AI users rating AI good or very good at complex tasks: 34.2% (2024), 36.8% (2025), 59.2% (2026, changed wording). Within each year, each extra point on the complexity rating is associated with about 2.2-2.4 times the odds of being favourable.

title: Perceived job threat 2024 vs 2025 by role and region
alt_text: Dumbbell chart. Share of professional AI users/planners who see AI as a threat to their job rose from 11.5% to 15.2%. Largest rises: Research / education +9.3; Student +7.5; Data / AI / analytics +6.3. Changes not significant after BH: Ops / infra / security / support, MENA, Afg. & Pakistan, Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Sensitivity of year-on-year changes to QC, standardisation, weighting and missing-data bounds
alt_text: Forest plot of year-on-year changes for use, favourability, trust and distrust under raw, standardised, QC-inclusive, strict-QC, completion-weighted and Manski-bound analyses. All point estimates keep the same sign. Manski bounds exclude zero for all contrasts except adoption 2024 to 2025 (-2.8 to 24.9 points).
